policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'chief officers' renders either the qere נִצָּבִים (niphal participle, those stationed as officers) or the ketiv נְצִיבִים (prefects/governors); both are officials over the people and the English does not distinguish them. No textual note on this verse. Base qere fallback retained.
Qere אֳנִיּוֹת and ketiv אוניות are defective vs plene spellings of the same word 'ships'; ASV 'ships' fits both identically. No textual note on this verse. Base qere fallback retained.
